messages:
Alex G: Heads-up — we need a short alignment on the ingest contract for the new per-route performance panels (latency P50/P95/P99, TTFT, tokens/sec). Console team wants consistent dimensions so dashboards can be templated. Maya / Jorge can you weigh in on runtime emission constraints?

Maya R: Thanks. Quick ask: console needs stable metric names + a few tags: route_id, model_family, model_version, region, deploy_id. Can runtime emit those without blowing cardinality?

Jorge L: We can emit those tags; model_version and deploy_id are optional at high QPS. For top-level SLOs we can emit full tags at sample rate. Suggest: emit exact tags for 100% of requests for latency percentiles but sample attributes for tokens/sec when > 5k rps.

Priya S: From Console POV, we need:
- metrics with predictable names
- ability to pivot by model_version (for rollouts)
- canary overlay support (show canary vs baseline on the same panel)
So stable names matter more than every single tag on every datapoint.

Sam T: +1. Ops concerns: histograms for P99 need raw buckets kept for at least 48h to calculate accurate percentiles across aggregations. If we sample too aggressively we lose P99 signal. Propose: full histogram at 1m granularity, TTL 7d. Sampled attributes ok for tokens/sec and labels.

Jorge L: Implementation plan from runtime: we will emit these metric families (naming conv):

```
request.latency_ms.count
request.latency_ms.sum
request.latency_ms.bucket  # prometheus-style histogram
request.ttft_ms.count
request.ttft_ms.sum
request.tokens_per_sec.avg
```

Attributes: route_id, model_family, model_version (optional), region, deploy_id (optional), tenant_id (when relevant). We'll add an `emission.sample_rate` tag to indicate sampling.

Maya R: Console expects: canonical metric names prefixed with `redwood.` (so dashboards can import easily). Can we namespace them? e.g. `redwood.request.latency_ms.bucket`

Jorge L: fine with `redwood.*`. We'll change the code paths to emit that prefix.

Priya S: For panel UX: standard panels we want:
- latency heatmap and p50/p95/p99 line series by route
- TTFT P50/P95 line series
- tokens/sec timeseries (avg and p95)
- request rate (rps)
- canary vs baseline stacked overlay with deploy_id filter
Also a lightweight per-route card showing current P95 and a green/yellow/red status based on SLO thresholds.

Alex G: Nice. Two policy questions: 1) default sampling for high QPS routes (Jorge suggested attr sampling) and 2) recommended aggregation windows (1m for raw ingest, 5m/15m for dashboards?).

Jorge L: Defaults:
- raw histograms: 1m rollup, keep buckets for 7d
- high QPS routes (>2000 rps): sample attributes at 1%, but emit histogram at 100% for latency only (we have fast path to compute latency histograms without full tag set).
- tokens/sec metrics: aggregate on runtime to 1s then rollup to 1m for ingest.

Sam T: Alerting guidance: fire once P95 > threshold for 5m sustained OR P99 spike > 2x baseline for 1m. Also create quota alerts if tokens/sec bursts exceed committed capacity.

Priya S: For rollouts UX, console will expose a dropdown to pin `model_version` and a toggle to show canary overlay. To make this work, queries need a `deploy_id` tag and consistent model_version formatting (semver-ish).

Maya R: One last thing — tagging convention: use snake_case for tag keys, no spaces, model_version as `model_version="v1.2.3"` or `model_version="canary-20240612"`. Please document allowed characters.

Jorge L: Agreed; we'll enforce tag sanitization: replace whitespace with `_`, truncate tags >128 chars, and send `tag_normalization` header in telemetry metadata.

telemetry-bot: Automatic note: schema v1.4 will include `redwood.*` names, attributes: route_id, model_family, model_version, region, deploy_id, tenant_id, emission.sample_rate. Histograms retained 7d. See: https://go/internal/telemetry/schema/v1.4

Alex G: Action items:
- Jorge: land runtime emitters with `redwood.` prefix + tag normalization (ETA: 2 weeks)
- Maya/Priya: draft dashboard templates (panels + canary overlay) using the new names (ETA: 1 week)
- Sam: draft alert rules and retention requirements (ETA: 3 business days)
- Jorge & Sam: confirm storage/ingest cost estimate for 7d histograms (ETA: 1 week)

Maya R: I'll start the dashboard PR and include example queries and templating variables.

Jorge L: Acknowledge. I'll open the runtime PR and link the config.

Priya S: Ack, will prototype overlay UX and share mocks.

Sam T: Ack. I'll run a quick cost calc and share numbers.

Alex G: Great — please drop PRs/links here and we'll close this thread after we have PRs linked. Thanks all :thumbsup:
